$comment: Screen registry for the ui-mock-diff skill. `mock` is relative to mocks/, `route` is the React route on the running dev server. A screen with route:null is mock-only (not implemented yet) and is skipped by the impl/diff steps.

screens.name: overview
screens.note: New. Summary of the four inbound surfaces, quota, spend, failover.

screens.name: routing
screens.note: Preference chain for one surface/scenario/lane. Absorbs RouterPreferences + TierEditor + RouterUtilization.

screens.name: routing-passthrough
screens.note: The passthrough half — today's hardcoded behaviour for chat/completions and responses, made visible and reversible.

screens.name: routing-map
screens.note: Graph editor. Absorbs RoutingLibrary + RoutingLiveEditor + RoutingPresetEditor. Adds the inbound-surface column.

screens.name: routing-rules
screens.note: Rule editor + tester. Replaces routing-map/RuleEditor.tsx.

screens.name: providers
screens.note: Subscription provider detail. Absorbs Subscriptions + SubscriptionAccountsPanel.

screens.name: providers-apikey
screens.note: API-key provider detail — key field, real prices, per-model apiStyle override.

screens.name: providers-connect
screens.note: Add-provider flow. Absorbs ConnectChoiceDialog + ProviderConnectFlow + ImportCredentialsDialog + ManualCallbackDialog. KNOWN DIFF ~15% dark: the mock draws step 2 of three, mid-authentication; the route opens on step 1. Capture limitation, not an implementation gap.

screens.name: providers-connect-models
screens.note: Step 3 of the add-provider flow (ConnectModelsStep), which the mock set stopped short of. Route is null because the step is a state of /providers/connect rather than its own path, so a capture would land on step 1.
screens.$comment: Reuses the provider detail model table on purpose: same decision, made before the provider takes traffic.

screens.name: activity
screens.note: Sessions tab. Absorbs Sessions + Usage + ApiCost.

screens.name: activity-requests
screens.note: Per-request log with Requested → Sent, matched rule and token attribution.

screens.name: activity-usage
screens.note: Usage tab. Subscription windows including the per-model weekly ones Overview drops, utilization over time, and per-token spend — previously visible only inside Settings -> Access. Reads /api/usage and /api/usage/history, neither of which had a UI reader before this. KNOWN DIFF ~5% light / ~6% dark: the mock draws two subscription accounts (six windows); a one-account install renders three, and the missing rows shift every section below them. Data, not design — the section order, heads and column layout line up.

screens.name: activity-session
screens.note: Session detail with the routing trace. Route stays null because /activity/sessions/:sessionId needs a real captured session id, which differs per install — a hardcoded one would shoot the not-found state.

screens.name: activity-logs
screens.note: Server log grouped by request id. Absorbs LogViewer and its four sub-components.

screens.name: settings
screens.note: Server section. Absorbs SettingsPage.

screens.name: settings-access
screens.note: Access tokens (Phase 3.5). KNOWN DIFF ~12%: the mock depicts an install with Cloudflare Access configured (signed-in email, populated policy rows); an install without it correctly renders the other state, including an exposure warning the mock is never in a position to show. State, not design — trimming copy does not move it.

screens.name: settings-access-token
screens.note: One token's own page: rotate, re-scope, revoke. Reached by clicking a row in Settings -> Access, which is where those actions used to live — as row actions they sat one mis-aimed click from every row of a table of live credentials. Route needs `bun run db:seed:demo`, whose token ids are deterministic; without it the capture lands on the not-found state.

screens.name: settings-logging
screens.note: Log level, request/message capture, retention per store.

screens.name: settings-personas
screens.note: Absorbs Personas + PersonaView + PersonaEdit — three routes for one object.

screens.name: settings-statusline
screens.note: Absorbs StatusLineConfigDialog + its six sub-components. Modal becomes a three-pane editor.

screens.name: settings-advanced
screens.note: Absorbs DebugPage + JsonEditor. Config document + danger zone.

screens.name: settings-advanced-health
screens.note: The Advanced screen's Health tab (GET /health, at the root so uptime checks need no token). The mock had the tab and nothing behind it. `skip` is a first-class result, not a failure.

screens.name: nav-accordion
screens.note: Proposal A for the two-vertical-menus problem: the active section expands in the sidebar and Settings loses its 13rem rail; Routing and Activity keep their tab strips. Drawn on Settings -> Server so A and B can be compared on the same screen. Mock-only until one proposal is picked.

screens.name: nav-drilldown
screens.note: Proposal B: the sidebar is replaced by the section's own items, with one row back up. Same screen as A. The trade to judge is that the other four sections leave the screen.

screens.name: nav-tree
screens.note: Proposal C: A applied everywhere, so the tab strips move into the sidebar too. Drawn on Activity -> Requests because that is the only place C differs from A; on a Settings screen the two are the same picture.

screens.name: nav-cloudflare
screens.note: Proposal D: C plus the two things that carry Cloudflare's own deep sidebar - a search field above the tree, and several groups open at once instead of only the current one. Sidebar 16rem. Drawn on Settings -> Server so it lines up with A and B.

screens.name: nav-collapsed
screens.note: Proposal E: what the FOLDED sidebar does with the second level. D won and the sidebar became the only navigation; folding it then dropped Activity's four views and Settings' six sections, which below 1024px (where it folds itself) left them reachable only through the command palette. The rail keeps its icons and the children arrive as a flyout. Mock-only: the collapsed state is a state of every screen, not a route the diff harness can visit.

screens.name: setup
screens.note: Absorbs SetupDialog. First-run explanation before the first question.

screens.name: system-states
screens.note: OAuth ok/error, 404, API-unreachable. Four routes shown together for tone comparison.
